line: **Sejjil (Ashura):** Iran's **two-stage solid-fuel medium-range ballistic missile**, launched for the first time against Israeli and US bases; range **2,500 km**, speed up to **Mach 13**; nicknamed the **"dancing missile"** for manoeuvring at high altitude to evade air defences.

mcq.s: The Sejjil ballistic missile, nicknamed the 'dancing missile', was developed by which country?
mcq.x: Sejjil (Ashura) is Iran's two-stage solid-fuel medium-range ballistic missile.

line: **Halometallurgy:** uses **halogens (mainly chlorine) or halogen salts** to recover critical metals like **lithium** from used lithium-ion batteries; a new halometallurgical method uses **common alkali salts** for **Li-ion battery recycling**.

**Recusal of a judge:** a judge withdraws from a case due to **conflict of interest or bias**; based on **nemo judex in causa sua**; India has **no specific (codified) provision** – the decision rests **solely with the judge**.

mcq.s: The principle of recusal of judges is based on which doctrine?
mcq.x: Recusal rests on nemo judex in causa sua (no one should be a judge in his own cause); India has no codified recusal law.

line: **Druzhba ('Friendship') pipeline:** among the world's longest crude oil pipeline networks (**~5,500 km**); starts at **Almetyevsk, Russia**, splits at **Mozyr (Belarus)** into a northern branch to **Germany** and a southern branch through **Ukraine**; Soviet-era, carries Russian crude to Europe.

mcq.s: The Druzhba pipeline, recently repaired by Ukraine, carries which commodity?
mcq.x: Druzhba ('Friendship') is a ~5,500 km Soviet-era crude oil pipeline from Russia to Europe.

line: **Tribal Ecological Communitarianism (TEC):** a socio-economic framework of **collective ownership, cooperative labour and equitable resource distribution** with **"ecological embeddedness"** – a sustainable alternative to profit-driven models; supported by **FRA (Gram Sabhas), PESA** and **Van Dhan Yojana**.

**Amchang WLS:** on the **eastern fringe of Guwahati, Assam**, bounded north by the **Brahmaputra**; an extension of Meghalaya's **Khasi and Jaintia Hills**; declared WLS in **2004**; Gauhati HC questioned tree felling for the **Guwahati Ring Road**.

mcq.s: Amchang Wildlife Sanctuary, in news over tree felling for a ring road project, is located in which state?
mcq.x: Amchang WLS lies on the eastern fringe of Guwahati, Assam (declared 2004).

line: **Market Coupling ('One Grid, One Price'):** CERC draft pools buy and sell bids from all power exchanges into a **single national pool**; **Grid Controller of India Ltd** is the sole **Market Coupling Operator**; one **Uniform Clearing Price**; initially for **Day-Ahead and Real-Time Markets**.

**Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) Tolling:** **barrier-free** electronic tolling without vehicles stopping; uses **RFID** (FASTag) and **ANPR cameras** (vehicle registration numbers); first at **Choryasi Fee Plaza (Gujarat)**.

mcq.s: Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling uses which technologies?
mcq.x: MLFF reads FASTags by RFID and captures registration numbers with ANPR cameras.

line: **Truck-Mounted Attenuators (TMAs):** impact-absorbing devices on trucks that protect **highway work zones** by absorbing collision energy; MoRTH deployed **33 TMAs across 9 NH projects**.

**Tunguska (NATO: SA-19 'Grison'):** **Soviet-origin** mobile self-propelled anti-aircraft system combining **surface-to-air missiles and guns** on one tracked chassis; **SHORAD**, 18 km detection radar; MoD signed a contract with **Russia** to procure it.

line: **Sijimali bauxite project:** clashes in **Rayagada, Odisha**; **Odisha** has **~41% of India's bauxite resources** and **~73% of production**; bauxite is the raw material for alumina and aluminium.
**Lyme disease:** vector-borne infection caused by the bacterium **Borrelia burgdorferi**; spread by bites of infected **black-legged ticks**; **not contagious**.

**Himalayan Salamander (Tylototriton himalayanus):** rare amphibian, one of **two salamander species in India** (other: Manipuri Newt); endemic to the **eastern Himalaya** (India, eastern Nepal, Bhutan); in India in **Darjeeling**.
**Asola Bhatti WLS:** invasive **Prosopis juliflora** has colonised **63.48%** of the sanctuary.

**Laokhowa–Burhachapori WLS (Assam):** twin protected ecosystem on the **Brahmaputra's southern bank**, connecting **Kaziranga and Orang National Parks**; fringe women turned **water hyacinth** into wealth.

mcq.s: Laokhowa–Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary connects which two National Parks?
mcq.x: It lies on the Brahmaputra's southern bank linking Kaziranga and Orang NPs.

line: **Afsluitdijk Dam:** **32-km** barrier dam and causeway in the **Netherlands** protecting low-lying land from **North Sea** floods; also for navigation, freshwater storage and renewable energy; PM visited it for water-management cooperation (useful for **Kalpasar**).

mcq.s: Afsluitdijk, visited by the Indian PM in 2026, is a
mcq.x: Afsluitdijk is a 32-km barrier dam and causeway in the Netherlands protecting against North Sea floods.

line: **Dhirauli coal mine (MP):** with **Urtan**, began production under commercial coal mining; Dhirauli is part of the **Singrauli coalfield**; both lie in the **Gondwana** rock system.
**Veer Gundadhur:** tribal leader born in **Netanar village, Bastar**, who led the **Bhumkal Rebellion (1910)** against British rule (forced labour, forest restrictions).

mcq.s: Veer Gundadhur led which tribal uprising against British rule?
mcq.x: Gundadhur of Netanar (Bastar) led the Bhumkal Rebellion of 1910.

line: **Risdiplam:** **oral drug** that slows or halts **Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)** – a rare genetic neuromuscular disorder; patients seek inclusion of its generic under the **National Policy for Rare Diseases**.
**Daraxonrasib:** novel **oral therapy** targeting common **RAS mutations** to treat **pancreatic cancer** (a KRAS inhibitor).
**Gotland:** strategically important **Swedish island in the Baltic Sea**; site of NATO exercises.

**Legal Personhood for Nature:** granting a river, forest, mountain or ecosystem the status of a **"legal person"** with enforceable rights, so **guardians** can file cases; debated for fragile **Himalayan and hill regions**.

**Synthetic Biology (SynBio):** combines **engineering with molecular biology** to design or build new biological parts and systems; unlike genetic engineering (single gene), it builds **multi-gene networks**; driven by CRISPR, AI, cheap DNA synthesis.
**Fortytwo Labs (Pune):** its **Ci2** became India's **first cryptographic algorithm** to get **C-SAFE** recognition from the **Data Security Council of India (DSCI)**.
**Vibe Coding:** AI-assisted software development where developers describe what they want in **natural language** and AI generates most of the code.
**Sufiyana Mousiqi:** classical music of **Kashmir** (14th–15th c.) rooted in **Sufi mysticism**; J&K proposed it for **UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage** list.
**2-Bromo-4-Methylpropiophenone:** notified as a **controlled substance under the NDPS Act** (Ministry of Finance) as a precursor for **mephedrone ('Meow Meow', M-CAT)**.

**Chloramphenicol and Nitrofurans:** banned in India (**March 2025**) in **aquaculture and food-producing animals**; action stepped up in **shrimp farming** after export rejections; chloramphenicol residues can cause **aplastic anaemia**.

line: **Rotavirus:** a genus in the family **Reoviridae**; leading cause of severe diarrhoea in **children under 5**; spreads by the **faecal-oral route**.

**Methamidophos and Acephate:** Chillies Exporters Association urged **Andhra Pradesh** to ban or restrict them in **export-oriented chilli**; methamidophos is a highly toxic **organophosphate**, WHO **Class Ib**, not approved for agricultural use in India.

mcq.s: Methamidophos and Acephate, which exporters urged Andhra Pradesh to restrict, are used on which crop?
mcq.x: The Chillies Exporters Association sought curbs on these pesticides in export-oriented chilli.

line: **CosmoCube:** proposed mission to study the **early universe** by detecting faint **radio signals** from over **13.5 billion years ago**, spending ~40 minutes on the **Moon's far side** each two-hour orbit.

**Port of Refuge:** APSEZ inaugurated **India's first Port of Refuge** for vessels in distress at **Dighi (west coast)** and **Gopalpur (east coast)**; tripartite MoU with **SMIT Salvage (Royal Boskalis)** and MERC.

**Kaleshwaram barrages:** Telangana steering committee to restore **Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla** barrages after **NDSA** found design flaws; Kaleshwaram (2019) is among the world's largest **multi-stage lift irrigation** projects.
**Deakin University (Australia):** MoU with **Telangana** for AI, creating the **Aikam-Deakin Hub** for research in intelligent technology.

**Shikshapatri exhibition:** **Bodleian Library, Oxford** (est. **1602**) is marking **200 years** of the Hindu text *Shikshapatri* by **Sahajanand Swami (Swaminarayan)**, written in **1826** in **Sanskrit**, **212 verses**.
**Basra Memorial (Iraq):** names of **33,000 Indian WWI soldiers** of the **Mesopotamia campaign** added via digital panels by the **Commonwealth War Graves Commission**.
**Danveer programme:** individuals and organisations can **donate computers to Gram Panchayats** through the **Meri Panchayat app**.
**VISTAS, Chennai:** India's **first AI-integrated vertical university campus** (July 2026), inaugurated by **Sridhar Vembu** (Zoho co-founder).
**Ecogen:** **IIT Kanpur** Centre of Excellence for **Green Hydrogen**, approved by **UP** under the UP Green Hydrogen Policy 2024 (via **UPNEDA**).
